description: Implement configuration parameters for: Build a Distributed Federated Machine Learning & Proximal Optimization module in pure Python across 10 atomic tasks: 1) in config.py define cluster hyperparameters NUM_CLIENTS = 10, DIRICHLET_ALPHA = 0.5, LOCAL_EPOCHS = 3, LEARNING_RATE = 0.05, MU_PROXIMAL = 0.01, and ROUNDS = 25; 2) in core.py implement synthetic non-IID Dirichlet partition generation generate_federated_partitions(n_samples, n_clients, alpha, seed); 3) in core.py implement local client SGD optimization with proximal loss regularizer client_local_train(weights, bias, client_X, client_y, epochs, lr, mu); 4) in core.py implement federated server aggregation train_and_evaluate(csv_out_path, seed) comparing baseline FedAvg against proposed Adaptive FedProx under 25% client straggler dropout, saving communication_rounds, final_accuracy, communication_overhead_kb, straggler_resilience_rate, and divergence_rate to results.csv; 5) in test_core.py implement invariant pytest unit tests verifying partition completeness, proximal loss reduction, and aggregation weight normalization; 6) in plot_results.py generate publication-ready dual-axis convergence and straggler comparison charts in figures/comparison_chart.pdf and .png; 7) in references.bib synthesize contemporary SOTA literature (2023-2026, min. 6-8 citations from NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, JMLR, e.g. McMahan 2017, Li 2020 FedProx, Wang 2023, Karimireddy 2024, Kairouz 2024, Zhao 2023); 8) in thesis.md author Chapters 1-3 (Intro, SOTA taxonomy with research gap, and TikZ distributed architecture diagram); 9) in thesis.md author Chapters 4-6 with symbolic pointers \ref_ast{config.py:NUM_CLIENTS}, \ref_ast{config.py:DIRICHLET_ALPHA}, \ref_ast{config.py:LOCAL_EPOCHS}, \ref_ast{config.py:MU_PROXIMAL}, \ref_ast{config.py:ROUNDS}, \ref_csv{results.csv:baseline:final_accuracy}, \ref_csv{results.csv:proposed:final_accuracy}, \ref_csv{results.csv:proposed:straggler_resilience_rate}, and \ref_fig{figures/comparison_chart.pdf}; 10) verify that all AST exports, CSV tables, and compiled thesis sections achieve 100% PASS in Layer 3.
